Grid¶

Human CSS provides the grid micro-attribute for CSS grid layout, complementing the existing flex micro-attribute.

Basic usage¶

Set up a grid container with a number of equal columns:

<div grid="three gap">
  <div>One</div>
  <div>Two</div>
  <div>Three</div>
</div>

Responsive grids¶

Use auto-fill or auto-fit for grids that adapt to available space. Control the minimum cell size with the --grid-min CSS variable (defaults to 10rem).

<div grid="auto-fit" gap="medium" style="--grid-min: 15rem">
  <div>Card</div>
  <div>Card</div>
  <div>Card</div>
  <div>Card</div>
</div>

auto-fill creates as many tracks as will fit, even if empty. auto-fit collapses empty tracks, allowing items to stretch.

Direction and density¶

By default, grid items flow by row. Use columns to flow by column, or dense to pack items tightly:

<div grid="three columns"></div>
<div grid="three dense"></div>

Alignment¶

Grid uses the same alignment keywords as flexbox:

<div grid="three center middle"></div>
<div grid="two justify"></div>

top, middle, bottom control vertical alignment. left, center, right control horizontal alignment. stretch stretches items in both directions. justify and justify-gap distribute space between or around columns.

Spanning¶

Grid children can span multiple columns or rows:

<div grid="four">
  <div span="two">Wide item</div>
  <div>Normal</div>
  <div>Normal</div>
  <div span-row="two">Tall item</div>
</div>

Subgrid¶

Children can inherit the parent grid’s tracks:

<div grid="three">
  <div grid="subgrid" span="two">
    <div>Aligned to parent grid</div>
    <div>Aligned to parent grid</div>
  </div>
</div>

Gap¶

The gap micro-attribute works with both grid and flex containers:

<div grid="three" gap="thick"></div>
<div flex="wrap" gap="thin"></div>

Gap sizes: thin (0.25em), medium (0.5em), thick (1em), x-thick (2em), or use any length with a number and unit. Use gap="row" or gap="column" to set gaps in only one direction.
